architectureSummary.ruleOwnership: State transitions, retry, resume, cancellation, destination conflict, finalization, recovery, and integrity policies are implemented once in the shared domain or service. Desktop UI, browser, network, persistence, filesystem, packaging, telemetry, and test adapters consume this contract and must not duplicate or redefine it.

dataSafetyInvariants: Completed is persisted only after successful content finalization.
Partial content is never exposed as a completed file.
Resume requires a valid range response and matching remote identity; otherwise an explicit restart outcome is presented.
Metadata transitions and filesystem finalization are recoverable across process termination.
Raw URLs, credentials, authorization data, cookies, local paths, filenames, and file contents are excluded from ordinary diagnostics.

operatorRunbook.production: Not declared or authorized. Production deployment and public distribution require separate attributed human approval.
startOfWorkChecks: Confirm a dated sepehr-product-owner decision approves the first platform, supported versions, primary segment, bounded MVP, exclusions, and meaning of native and all devices.
Confirm ADR-01 through ADR-04 have accountable approval or an explicit deferred status.
Confirm license, dependency rules, contribution governance, vulnerability reporting, release ownership, signing custody, and rollback ownership are approved before public distribution work.
Use generated non-sensitive fixtures, loopback or isolated test services, temporary destinations, and no production credentials or data.

incidentTriage.action: Load the durable record and partial-file facts through adapters, let the shared domain decide recoverability, and never force completed status.

incidentTriage.symptom: Server ignores or changes a range response
incidentTriage.action: Stop append behavior, preserve evidence without sensitive URL data, validate remote identity, and surface explicit restart or failure through the shared domain.

incidentTriage.symptom: Destination is full, locked, missing, or conflicts
incidentTriage.action: Keep partial content non-final, report the platform error through the filesystem port, and apply only the product-approved conflict or retry policy.
Quarantine ambiguous completion, retain recoverable metadata, run integrity reconciliation, and do not silently rename or delete user content.
Capture privacy-safe resource and latency measurements on the approved platform, reduce work through shared concurrency policy, and rerun real-runtime tests.

evidenceToCapture: package install, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall results
escalation: Product-scope ambiguity goes to sepehr-product-owner; engineering must not infer approval.
Architecture, integrity, privacy, or security failures block packaging and distribution.
Only ENG-15 may issue the independent engineering verification disposition.

principles: Every schema change is versioned, forward-tested, rollback-planned, and compatible with recoverable partial downloads.
Back up or atomically preserve metadata before transformation; never use destructive production operations.
Migrations do not mutate downloaded content unless an approved, integrity-checked file operation requires it.
Unknown or invalid records are quarantined for explicit recovery rather than silently discarded.
A failed migration leaves the prior readable state or a tested recovery copy.
preMigration: Verify free space and recovery destination
Create and validate a recoverable metadata copy
Inventory active and partial downloads without logging sensitive fields
execution: Apply one idempotent version step at a time
Validate state values and transition invariants
Reconcile metadata with partial and finalized files through the shared service
Record counts and non-sensitive error categories
postMigration: Reopen through the same repository adapter used by the application
Verify completed files are never downgraded or partial files promoted
Retain rollback evidence for the approved period
migrationGuidance.rollbackTrigger: Any parse failure, invariant violation, lost record, checksum mismatch, unexpected content mutation, or inability to reopen the migrated store.
migrationGuidance.limitation: No database engine, schema, migration tool, or executable repository exists, so this is operating guidance rather than an executed migration.

implementationNotes: This workstream adds documentation only and does not change user-visible behavior, source code, dependencies, schemas, infrastructure, or deployment state.
The repository currently contains planning artifacts and a planning-evidence validator, but no application source, executable download service, package manifest, lockfile, CI workflow, or runtime.
Business rules must be implemented once in the shared download domain or service and consumed by every UI and adapter.
Documentation must be updated with exact approved commands, versions, owners, supported platforms, and recovery steps when implementation choices become canonical.
No branch, commit, production credential, production data, destructive database operation, deployment, signing, or public release is part of this guide.
knownRisks: Primary segment, first platform, supported versions, bounded MVP, differentiation, exclusions, and meaning of all devices remain unapproved.
Discovery evidence and a dated human product decision are absent from the engineering planning package.
No executable implementation exists, so security, resilience, accessibility, performance, compatibility, and integrity outcomes are unverified.
Persistence and UI technology are undecided, so migration and command procedures remain templates.
License, dependency policy, governance, vulnerability reporting, signing custody, release ownership, and rollback ownership block public distribution.
Incorrect range or remote-identity handling can silently corrupt content unless adversarial integration tests enforce the shared invariants.
Independent engineering verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
